items.title: A particle made of force: physicists say they’ve found mysterious ‘glueball’
items.summary: Scientists have predicted the existence of a particle made of gluons for a long time, but detecting it has taken decades.

items.title: Glucose-responsive probiotics for glycaemic modulation in mice and monkeys
items.summary: Engineered probiotics equipped with a synthetic glucose-responsive circuit transiently colonize the gut and secrete therapeutic factors when glucose levels increase, enabling safe, oral, sense-and-respond control of diabetes in mouse and primate models.

items.title: A gas-enshrouded and gas-reddened black hole at cosmic dawn
items.summary: Observations of an unusual cosmic-dawn source illuminate how early supermassive black holes may have grown rapidly in a gas-enshrouded state; such enshrouded black holes may lie at the heart of the 'little red dots'.

items.title: Superconducting 2D cuprate with a single CuO<sub>2</sub> plane
items.summary: A high-quality, pristine monolayer cuprate superconductor with a single CuO2 plane is fabricated and used to identify two quantum critical phenomena emerging between the Mott insulating phase and the superconducting phase.

items.title: In vivo genome-wide CRISPR screens of human T cells in solid tumours
items.summary: An in vivo model that is able to recover human T cells from solid tumours can identify targets to help improve CAR T cell antitumour activity.

items.title: Ultrafast temporal engineering of optical properties using terahertz light
items.summary: A photonic time crystal is an optical system of which properties such as its refractive index are modulated strongly and rapidly over time. One has now been obtained all-optically by delivering an intense terahertz light wave onto a material with a specialized microstructure that hosts collective waves of electrons known as plasmons.

items.title: Lead carboxylates passivation for meter-scale perovskite solar modules
items.summary: Lead carboxylates passivation for meter-scale perovskite solar modules

items.title: The probiotic bacteria engineered to treat diabetes
items.summary: Genetically modified bacteria lower high blood-sugar in animal trials — plus, how to watch a solar eclipse safely.

items.title: Procognitive restoration of PV neuron plasticity in neurodevelopmental disorders
items.summary: Expression of Meis2 in hippocampal parvalbumin-expressing interneurons in an adult mouse model of neurodevelopmental disorders rescues experience-dependent plasticity, improves memory and network function and suppresses seizures.

items.title: Luminescent-reaction-enabled super-resolution imaging
items.summary: A new chemistry-based super-resolution imaging framework is described, enabling 3D, laser-free, highly sensitive and ultralong-term imaging of live cells which overcomes the limitations in spatiotemporal resolution associated with reaction-based imaging methods.

items.title: Evidence for the first globular cluster stellar stream beyond the Milky Way
items.summary: Deep Hubble Space Telescope imaging of the ultra-diffuse galaxy UGC 9050-Dw1 reveals an extragalactic globular cluster stream, with analysis and modelling probing the rich dark matter content of the host galaxy.

items.title: Human brain stimulation engages different gene programs in different cell types
items.summary: Electrical stimulation of the human brain is a promising strategy for slowing cognitive decline. The discovery of cell-type-specific gene programs that are induced in tandem with the activity of networks of neurons in the temporal cortex when it is stimulated could inform the development of therapeutic approaches using stimulation.

items.title: Giant balloon gives rise to new view of the Milky Way’s centre
items.summary: Airborne camera gathers data about the high-energy particles emanating from the core of our Galaxy.

items.title: Temporal uncoupling of radial glia lineage progression in cortical organoids
items.summary: RGP lineage tracing in stem-cell-derived organoids shows highly plastic proliferation and reduced clonal neuronal diversity, indicating that missing non-cell-autonomous niche cues are essential for faithful temporal control of cortical lineage progression.

items.title: Rb-driven transcription limits its tumour-suppressive effects in breast cancer
items.summary: CDK4/6 inhibition redirects Rb chromatin occupancy to activate oestrogen-responsive genes, counteracting its own ability to maintain therapeutic cell-cycle arrest.

items.title: Degree-of-polarization modulation for high-dimensional optical computing
items.summary: By engineering the statistics of light at the micrometre scale using phase-only spatial light modulators, both the state and degree of polarization become spatially programmable, enabling direct encoding of information in a high-dimensional space.

items.title: Structural mechanism governing the directionality of bridge recombination
items.summary: Cryo-electron microscopy structures show how IS621 bridge recombinase mediates DNA excision, explaining its natural preference for insertion and informing the design of programmable bridge-editing technologies.

items.title: Maternal influences on infant gut microbiome and health
items.summary: The maternal gut microbiome is a predictor of infant eczema.

items.title: Biomarkers of nivolumab benefit in resectable non-small cell lung cancer
items.summary: Potential predictive biomarkers of perioperative nivolumab therapy benefit in non-small cell lung cancer are identified from evaluable participants in the CheckMate 77T trial.

items.title: A controversial Alzheimer’s surgery is said to reverse symptoms — here’s what scientists know
items.summary: Jaw-dropping patient videos and miraculous testimonials ignited a frenzy in China over a technique that aims to improve drainage from the brain. Now it is entering trials worldwide.

items.title: Rattlesnakes’ own anti-venom could protect humans too
items.summary: A mixture of proteins in snake blood can prevent the death of mice injected with an otherwise lethal dose of venom.

items.title: Shared principles of human and bacterial antiviral immunity
items.summary: The Review describes shared ancient, conserved mechanisms between human antiviral immunity and bacterial anti-phage systems, outlining universal principles of pathogen sensing, signalling and effector function that reveal common rules governing host–virus interactions across life.

items.title: Neural basis of compositional control
items.summary: Behaviour of human participants in a prey-pursuit task reflects dynamic blending of goal-specific control policies, with hippocampus estimating latent states, anterior cingulate cortex orchestrating policy switches and orbitofrontal cortex supplying value-based contextualization rather than driving continuous policy updating.

items.title: Species intraspecific variation drives tropical forest drought resistance
items.summary: Substantial intraspecific variation, together with species turnover, drives coordinated shifts in drought resistance such as increased embolism resistance and wider stomatal safety margins in drier forests.

items.title: How the human brain can pursue two goals at the same time
items.summary: In the natural world, an animal can blend strategies so it can advance towards several goals at the same time. An engineering approach called control theory was used to infer people’s goals while they played a simple video game, and showed how three brain regions work together to implement goal blending.

items.title: Bow shocks reveal how a dying star returns matter to interstellar space
items.summary: Deep imaging of ionized gas in the Helix Nebula uncovers many curved shock waves around a dying Sun-like star. These ‘bow shocks’ are produced when ejected shells of stellar material break up and race outwards. Their changing shapes imply that the shell fragments are being stripped, shredded and mixed into interstellar gas over roughly 10,000 years.

items.title: Cascading continental-scale floods across Europe in 1342–1343
items.summary: Tracing cascading continental-scale medieval megafloods across Europe indicates that current flood management is unprepared for such sequences, highlighting the urgent need for proactive flood risk management strategies that account for unusual series of extreme flood events.

items.title: Numerous bow shocks in the outer Helix Nebula
items.summary: Shocks in the eastern outskirts of the Helix Nebula, detected in Hα emission with the MOTHRA telescope, provide evidence for the recycling of fragmented stellar ejecta into the surrounding gas.

items.title: Heterogeneous climatic controls on tropical-forest biomass
items.summary: An analysis of the relationships between aboveground biomass and various climatic factors in three major regions of tropical forest shows that understanding the complex interactions between climate, topography and soils is crucial to predict how climate change will affect carbon storage capacity.

items.title: Intraspecific variation in tropical trees can drive resistance to drought
items.summary: Different tropical tree species can vary in their ability to withstand drought — and so too, it seems, can distinct populations of the same tree species.

items.title: Ocean temperatures set to break all-time record: what’s next?
items.summary: High sea surface temperatures are expected to weaken ocean carbon sinks and damage coral reefs.

items.title: No single rule explains how climate affects carbon storage in tropical forests
items.summary: Ecologists have long wondered why some tropical forests store more carbon than others. A global satellite survey offers an explanation.

items.title: Shipping on rivers packs a surprisingly large climate punch
items.summary: Growing traffic on inland waterways could offer an opportunity for cutting emissions.

items.title: Agentic profiles for effective AI governance
items.summary: A framework comprising four dimensions—autonomy, efficacy, goal complexity and generality—is proposed for characterizing AI agents, supporting the construction of agentic profiles for the effective governance of different AI agents.

items.title: Trump wants MMR vaccine split up: the science behind why it’s a bad idea
items.summary: Numerous studies have shown that separating childhood jabs will delay protection and increase costs for families.

items.title: Phosphine-mediated azine C–H couplings with water and ammonia
items.summary: Phosphine-mediated azine C–H couplings with water and ammonia

items.title: Towards an equitable future of global photovoltaic waste recycling
items.summary: Global photovoltaic waste will reach 297–402 million tonnes by 2060, and regionally adapted recycling strategies and international cooperation will be needed to provide equitable and scalable PV waste circularity.

items.title: ‘Little red dot’ gets its colour from gas — not dust
items.summary: Dust can tint the cosmos red, but a compact astronomical object is coloured by turbulent gas around a black hole.

items.title: How to make your science business succeed when you’re a female founder
items.summary: Sexist assumptions and a male-dominated culture can make it harder for women to attract investment for the companies they set up.
